title: introduce-tenant-bootstrap-credential-carrier-and-overlay-rewriter
author: Asha Kumar
description: Motivation: when installing Redwood Private in constrained VPC/on-prem environments customers often need a compact, idempotent path to seed tenant credentials and bootstrap small clusters without running the full init wave. This PR adds a credential-carrier component and an overlay-rewriter templating helper to the helm chart so operators can declaratively preseed credentials, transform overlay fragments for mirror/air-gapped registries, and opt into a transactional bootstrap mode. Summary: 1) new values schema fields under 'credentialCarrier' and 'overlayRewriter' (see values.schema.json) 2) a lightweight Deployment template (credential-carrier) that can run as init or sidecar depending on mode 3) templating helper functions to rewrite imagePullSecrets, registry mirrors and KMS provider blocks based on overlays 4) explicit migration notes and a safe default (credential seeding disabled) Checklist: - [x] values.schema.json updated and validated with helm schema linter - [x] unit tests for tpl helpers added - [x] smoke e2e in minikube for transactional and idempotent modes - [x] security scan for secret-in-transit mitigations - [x] docs/upgrade-note added Migration notes: existing users are unaffected by default; to opt-in set credentialCarrier.enabled=true and choose mode: "transactional" or "idempotent". transactional will run a single at-most-once seed attempt with a leader lock while idempotent runs a reconcile loop suitable for manual retries. Rollout plan: merged to main behind feature flag, gate in release notes, staged rollout to private-installer pipelines for three customer clusters before general availability. Backout: setting credentialCarrier.enabled=false disables the Deployment and any in-cluster seeding; seeds that already wrote credentials are left untouched and documented in upgrade-note.
commits: Initial values.schema.json and helper functions; add credential-carrier deployment template; add overlay-rewriter tpl helpers and tests; add docs/upgrade-note.md and changelog entry; fix linting and update schema examples
diff_snippets: +++ charts/redwood-private/values.schema.json: added 'credentialCarrier' object (enabled, mode, image, kmsProvider, preseed)
+++ charts/redwood-private/templates/_overlay_rewriter.tpl: new helper 'overlayRewriter.rewriteImage' to normalize mirror overlays
+++ charts/redwood-private/templates/credential-carrier-deployment.yaml: new Deployment with optional leader-lock sidecar for transactional mode

Author replies: implemented Lease API with 30s renew and 2m TTL, added dryRun boolean, and clarified schema descriptions. merge_outcome: merged via squash: 'credential-carrier: add bootstrap credential carrier and overlay rewriter helpers'
release_notes: charts/redwood-private: Add optional 'credentialCarrier' for declarative tenant credential seeding and 'overlayRewriter' helpers for registry/mirror transformations. Disabled by default. Provides transactional (leader-locked once) and idempotent reconcile modes. See docs/upgrades/credential-carrier-upgrade-note.md for migration steps and rollback guidance.
testing_instructions: To try locally: 1) helm template charts/redwood-private -f values.yaml.example --set credentialCarrier.enabled=true --set credentialCarrier.mode=idempotent | kubectl apply -f - 2) observe credential-carrier logs and confirm KMS provider is not invoked unless preseed.kmsProvider is set 3) run scripts/ci/helm-schema-validate.sh to verify values.schema.json 4) optional: enable dryRun to validate overlay transformations without writing secrets
notes_for_operators: credentialCarrier defaults to disabled. If using air-gapped registries, prefer overlayRewriter.overlays to map internal mirrors and set imagePullSecrets via secretRef in values to avoid plaintext in values files. For high-security installs use an external KMS and set credentialCarrier.preseed.kmsProvider to 'external' to avoid persisting plaintext credentials in-cluster.
